title: Fugaro shared-image lock
description: The installation's shared images, at builds/image-lock.json in the runs bucket (docs/forge-authorship-images/shared-images.md §3). It is the one source of every repository's image digest: each entry is one image, keyed by the normalised dependency set it was built from, and a repository's job is pointed at an entry's digest. Only the operator's machine writes it — `fugaro image refresh` after a successful build, `fugaro image prune` when it removes an entry — and it is decoded strictly (internal/imagecheck.ParseLock): an unknown field anywhere and a version other than 1 are refused, because every operator's machine writes this one object and every fugaro version in use reads it, so a reader that ignored a field it did not know would drop it for everyone on its next write.

version.description: The lock's own version (imagecheck.LockVersion). A reader that meets a version it does not know stops and names it rather than rewriting the object.

images.description: The installation's images, keyed by the normalised dependency-set key (imagecheck.Key): the same key is the same dependency set, and so the same image.

image.$comment: No property is required here, and that is deliberate: §3.2's strictness is about fields and the version, not presence. TestLockSchemaAgreesWithTheDecoder (internal/imagecheck) holds this schema and the decoder to the same documents; the three differences it pins are that a version written as 1.0 or 1e0 is the number 1 to a schema that reads numbers by value and a type error to encoding/json, that a null where an array or an object is expected is an absent field to encoding/json and refused here, and that the decoder refuses a lock placing one job on two entries, a rule about two entries at once that no schema validating one entry can state (see jobs). The writer always writes every property — the Go type has no pointer fields — so a required list would only be met by documents the writer never produces.

key.description: The image's normalised dependency-set key, the property of images it is stored under.

image.description: The image in the installation's shared registry repository, without a tag.

digest.description: The sha256:… the build promoted. An entry's digest is never overwritten in place: a changed dependency set is a changed key and so a new entry.

base_ref.description: The base the build ran FROM, as the build record's base_ref holds it.

base_digest.description: The sha256:… of the base the build ran FROM.

packages.description: This image's own resolved packages, one per fact: the name, the version and the integrity the key file stated for that version's artifact, each as a quoted string literal with one space between them (§2.4 of the design), the third written empty when the file stated none. A reuse (§4) is decided from these: an entry holds a repository's set when every one of its packages is here with the same three fields, and the entry may hold more.

tools.description: This image's own toolchain pins, as tool@version. §4 does not superset them: an entry is reused only when its tools are identical.

built_at.description: When the image was built. It breaks a tie between two entries with the same number of extra packages (§4).

build_id.description: The build that made the image.

jobs.description: The same set as repositories, each repository's job name as it was at update time. A job — one repository and one workflow — is on at most one entry of the whole lock: the decoder refuses a lock that places one on two (ParseLock's checkOneJobPerEntry, a rule about two entries at once that this schema cannot state), because a launch asking which image a job is on would otherwise answer with whichever entry it met first, and a job runs one image.

last_used_at.description: The last time a refresh placed a repository on this image. §9's age is measured from it.
